name: Hermetica USDh
oneLiner: USDh is Hermetica's BTC-backed synthetic dollar on Stacks, kept near $1 by pairing spot BTC long with equal-size short BTC perpetual futures positions on CEXes.
collateral: Dual yield-engine backing: BTC spot holdings paired with equal short BTC perpetual futures positions on centralized exchanges (delta-neutral), plus STRC digital-credit exposure added in 2026 (Saturn USDat route with Galaxy execution and Clear Street custody, and tokenized STRCx via Backed Assets/Kraken); BTC margin reserves custodied off-exchange via Copper (Clearloop) and Ceffu (MirrorX), with monthly custodian attestations of assets, liabilities and reserve coverage
pegMechanism: Delta-neutral hedging: BTC spot long + equal BTC short perpetual futures neutralize directional exposure; mint and redeem via KYC-gated Hermetica app; DIA oracle provides reserve-backed fair value pricing on Stacks

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Stacks transaction 0x6294eebb5e5560d8293268e2c28d3e9533d890007d8a573be80beb8b0db9ad49 deployed the exact tracked usdh-token-v1 contract at block 166,579 on September 19, 2024. Hermetica's official USDh documentation describes the matched BTC spot-long and perpetual-short backing strategy, supporting the synthetic-delta-neutral archetype.

oracleRisk.summary: USDh is issuer-minted from deposited USDC or USDT and backed by a centrally operated BTC basis strategy; Hermetica may pause redemptions when valuation feeds fail but does not expose a borrower-liquidation oracle path.

branchApplicability.rationale: Hermetica issues USDh directly to approved participants against USDC or USDT deposits and manages a protocol-level BTC/perpetual hedge. Users do not open collateralized debt positions, so there are no market-specific collateral-health or liquidation branches to inventory.

reserveReview.rationale: Write-time re-open 2026-07-30 of the June 2026 custodian attestation (snapshot 2026-06-30 17:00 UTC): USDh supply $2,465,576.78 against total backing assets $2,576,981.22 (103.92% coverage), split Ethereum Settlement Wallet $2,303,829.94 (89.4%), Stacks Redeeming Reserve $101,765.77 (4.0%), Reserve Fund $114,244.22 (4.4%: USDC $100,148.12 = 3.9% and USDh $14,096.10 = 0.5%), Copper $57,141.30 (2.2%), Ceffu $0.00, Mint Wallet $0.00. Slice weights are computed from these attested figures. Since the March 2026 snapshot the Ceffu balance went to zero and most backing moved to the Ethereum Settlement Wallet, whose contents the attestation does not itemize; Hermetica's April and July 2026 disclosures document new STRC digital-credit backing routes (Saturn USDat with Galaxy execution and Clear Street custody; tokenized STRCx issued by Backed Assets (JE) Limited via Kraken xStocks) that settle on Ethereum. The Reserve Fund's USDh portion is a circular exposure to the protocol's own token. Hermetica's backing docs still describe the delta-neutral BTC basis hedge and Copper/Ceffu off-exchange custody design.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Hermetica's monthly custodian attestations identify the venue-level allocation (Copper, Ceffu, Stacks Redeeming Reserve, Ethereum Settlement Wallet, Reserve Fund) but do not publish per-venue contents, account-level segregation, or insolvency terms; the STRC disclosures name Galaxy (execution) and Clear Street (custody) for the Saturn USDat route and Backed Assets (JE) Limited/Kraken for STRCx without disclosing shares; collateral is actively deployed as futures margin and credit exposure, so reuse within the strategy is inherent.

mintAuthority.summary: USDh mints only after a two-step backend attestation: a KYC-whitelisted minter calls request-mint and deposits BTC, then Hermetica's trader opens the delta-neutral hedge off-chain and calls confirm-mint to release USDh, making supply gated by Hermetica's off-chain operator.

controls.label: Hermetica hq-v1 minting contracts (confirm-mint operators)

routeChecks.signingModel: USDh minting is two-step: KYC-whitelisted minter request/deposit first, then Hermetica confirm-mint operators release USDh after off-chain hedge execution.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: hq-v1 minting-contracts map limits active mint routes to reviewed contracts; no permissionless mint path exists.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: New minting contracts and owner changes are subject to the hq-v1 1008-block timelock.

controls.evidence: Hiro API read of hq-v1 minting-contracts map: two contracts are currently active — minting-otc-v1-1 (burn-block-height=some(927047)) and emergency-recover-v1 (burn-block-height=some(862013)), both deployed by SPN5AKG35QZSK2M8GAMR4AFX45659RJHDW353HSG (Hermetica deployer). minting-otc-v1-1 is the primary OTC minting route; emergency-recover-v1 is an emergency recovery contract. minting-auto-v1-1 was deactivated 2026-03-23 and removed. No permissionless mint path exists.
controls.capDescription: minting-otc-v1-1 confirm-mint is bounded by a rolling mint-limit (live: 1,000,000 USDh per 1,200s window); set-mint-limit asserts new-limit <= the max-mint-limit constant (1,000,000 USDh), so the confirm-mint operators cannot raise the ceiling.

controls.label: hq-v1 owner (SM1QXYXZG... — Stacks P2SH/multisig address)

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: hq-v1 owner is a Stacks P2SH/multisig address and owner changes/new minting contracts use a 1008-block timelock.
routeChecks.unsupportedReason: Stacks P2SH signer set and threshold were not enumerated on-chain.

controls.evidence: Hiro API get-owner read on hq-v1: owner data-var returns Clarity bytes 0x05146fdf77f03a1ace4bf29f8090067a98c65000e1e2, decoded via c32check (version byte 20 = SM P2SH/multisig prefix) to SM1QXYXZG78DCWJZJKY0901KTK3350071W9YYRPMT. This is a Stacks P2SH multisig address (SM prefix) — signers and threshold not enumerated on-chain. Ownership transferred from deployer SP1N0K23NJTRK19SV9BFP8SVXQQFQ7XGGBFJ8DBVX via 2-step timelock (request-owner-update nonce 24, activate-next-owner nonce 25, executed 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-10). hq-v1 enforces a 1008-block (~7 day) timelock on owner changes and minting-contract additions.
controls.capDescription: hq-v1 owner can register and activate a new minting contract with any cap (1,008 burn-block timelock) and can set-contract-active a protocol contract that calls minting-otc-v1-1.set-mint-limit, so the effective mint ceiling is owner-raiseable.

controls.label: Minter whitelist (KYC/KYB gate)

routeChecks.signingModel: Only KYC/KYB-approved participants can request direct mints/redemptions; Hermetica administers this off-chain whitelist.
routeChecks.unsupportedReason: The off-chain whitelist administration process and signer controls are issuer-operated and not enumerated on-chain.

controls.evidence: Only KYC/KYB-approved participants whitelisted by Hermetica can request mints/redemptions directly; access to the mint route is administered off-chain by the issuer.
controls.capDescription: The minter whitelist gates who may request a mint (minting-state-v1 whitelist map, whitelist-enabled = true); it carries no cap-setting function.

review.evidence: Hiro API reads on hq-v1 (SPN5AKG35QZSK2M8GAMR4AFX45659RJHDW353HSG.hq-v1): (1) owner = SM1QXYXZG78DCWJZJKY0901KTK3350071W9YYRPMT (SM-prefix P2SH multisig, transferred 2026-02-10 via 1008-block timelock); (2) active minting-contracts: minting-otc-v1-1 (primary OTC route) and emergency-recover-v1, both deployed by Hermetica deployer; minting-auto-v1-1 deactivated 2026-03-23. No permissionless mint path. hq-v1 enforces 7-day timelock on owner changes and new minting-contract activations. Minting model confirmed as backend-attested OTC with a multisig-governed admin layer.
